questions.stem: Which plant division is characterised by the production of seeds that are enclosed within a fruit?
questions.explanation: Angiosperms are the flowering plants; after fertilisation the ovary wall develops into a fruit that encloses and protects the seeds. The fruit also assists dispersal, which is one reason angiosperms are the most widespread plant group.

distractorRationale.a: Bryophytes such as mosses produce no seeds at all, only spores
distractorRationale.b: Ferns also reproduce by spores rather than seeds
distractorRationale.c: Gymnosperms produce seeds but they are naked, borne on cone scales with no fruit

questions.stem: Mosses are restricted to damp, shaded habitats mainly because they

options.text: have no chlorophyll and cannot make food in bright light
lack vascular tissue and need a film of water for their sperm to reach the egg
produce seeds that only germinate in the dark
have a taproot that cannot penetrate dry soil

questions.explanation: Without xylem and phloem a moss cannot transport water efficiently, so it must stay small and close to a moist surface. Its male gametes are also flagellated and swim, so fertilisation fails unless there is a surface film of water.

distractorRationale.a: Mosses are green and photosynthesise normally
distractorRationale.d: Mosses have no true roots at all, only rhizoids

questions.stem: A maize seedling has one seed leaf, leaves with parallel veins and a fibrous root system. It is therefore
questions.explanation: One cotyledon, parallel venation and fibrous roots are the three standard monocot features and they occur together. A dicot such as cowpea would show two cotyledons, net-like veins and a taproot.

distractorRationale.b: Dicots have two seed leaves, net venation and a taproot
distractorRationale.c: Gymnosperms bear naked seeds in cones and have no cotyledon-based classes of this kind
distractorRationale.d: Pteridophytes are ferns and produce no seeds, so they have no cotyledons

questions.stem: An animal has a chitinous exoskeleton, a body divided into head, thorax and abdomen, three pairs of jointed legs and one pair of antennae. It belongs to the class
questions.explanation: Three pairs of legs, three distinct body regions and one pair of antennae together identify an insect. Leg count is the quickest test: insects have six legs, arachnids eight, crustaceans ten or more, and myriapods a pair or two per segment.

distractorRationale.a: Arachnids such as spiders have four pairs of legs, two body regions and no antennae
distractorRationale.c: Crustaceans such as crabs have two pairs of antennae and many more legs
distractorRationale.d: Myriapods such as millipedes have a long body of many similar segments, each bearing legs

questions.stem: The earthworm is placed in the phylum Annelida because its body is

options.text: long and divided into many similar segments

questions.explanation: Annelids are the segmented worms: the body consists of a series of similar rings, each with its own set of bristles called chaetae. Segmentation is the diagnostic feature that separates them from flatworms and roundworms.

distractorRationale.a: A flat unsegmented body describes Platyhelminthes such as the tapeworm
distractorRationale.c: A calcareous shell is a feature of Mollusca such as the snail
distractorRationale.d: Jointed limbs are the defining feature of Arthropoda

questions.stem: A bat flies, yet biologists place it in the class Mammalia rather than Aves. Which pair of features justifies this?

options.text: It lays eggs and has a beak
It has hair on its body and suckles its young on milk
It is warm-blooded and has a four-chambered heart
It has wings and a light skeleton

questions.explanation: Hair and mammary glands are unique to mammals, so they are the diagnostic features. Flight is a way of life that has evolved separately in insects, birds, bats and extinct reptiles, so it cannot be used to define a class.

distractorRationale.a: Bats give birth to live young and have teeth, not a beak
distractorRationale.c: Birds are also warm-blooded with a four-chambered heart, so this does not separate the classes
distractorRationale.d: Wings occur in both bats and birds, so they cannot distinguish the two

questions.stem: Which vertebrate class is characterised by dry horny scales and eggs with leathery shells laid on land?
questions.explanation: Reptiles were the first vertebrates fully independent of water: dry scaly skin cuts water loss and the leathery shelled egg allows development on land. Lizards, snakes, tortoises and crocodiles all share these features.

distractorRationale.a: Fish have wet scales and lay soft eggs in water
distractorRationale.b: Amphibians have moist naked skin and lay jelly-covered eggs in water
distractorRationale.d: Birds have feathers and lay eggs with hard, chalky shells

questions.stem: A snail is classified as an arthropod because it has a hard shell.
questions.explanation: False. A snail belongs to the phylum Mollusca: it has a soft, unsegmented body and a muscular foot, and its shell is made of calcium carbonate. Arthropods are defined by jointed limbs and a chitinous exoskeleton, neither of which a snail has.

questions.stem: Which invertebrate phylum contains animals with a sac-like body, a single body opening and tentacles bearing stinging cells?
questions.explanation: Coelenterates such as Hydra and jellyfish have a hollow sac body with one opening that serves as both mouth and anus, and a ring of tentacles armed with stinging cells for capturing prey. They are also radially symmetrical.

distractorRationale.a: Nematodes are cylindrical worms with a mouth and an anus and no tentacles
distractorRationale.c: Annelids are segmented and have a complete gut with two openings
distractorRationale.d: Molluscs have a muscular foot and usually a shell, and no stinging tentacles

questions.stem: A specimen has true roots, stems and leaves with vascular tissue, but bears no flowers and no seeds. Brown patches containing spores are found on the underside of its leaves. Identify the division, give two reasons for your answer, and state two ways it differs from a flowering plant.
markingGuide: Division correctly identified as Pteridophyta, that is a fern (2 marks)
Reason 1: it possesses vascular tissue with true roots, stems and leaves, which excludes Bryophyta (2 marks)
Reason 2: it reproduces by spores borne in sporangia on the underside of the fronds, which excludes seed plants (2 marks)
Difference 1: the fern produces spores whereas the flowering plant produces seeds (1 mark)
Difference 2: the fern has no flowers or fruits, so no pollination or fruit formation occurs; accept also that fern fertilisation needs external water while angiosperm fertilisation does not (1 mark)
questions.explanation: The combination of vascular tissue with spore reproduction is unique to the ferns, so the presence of xylem rules out mosses while the absence of seeds rules out gymnosperms and angiosperms. The differences from a flowering plant should contrast spores against seeds and the absence of flowers and fruit.
